description: State of charge, power and stored energy for the NEM battery fleet, driven by AEMO: the daily Next_Day_Dispatch ENERGY_STORAGE anchor integrated with 5-minute Dispatch_SCADA MW for the live per-unit inference, plus AEMO's own measured MW and region-level reported storage. OpenElectricity supplies the fleet's registered capacity, names and status (metadata only) plus its own API-budget metrics - its per-unit SOC/power families were retired when AEMO coverage proved a superset. The board is the whole AEMO fleet as NEMWEB reports it (every unit AEMO publishes, NEM only, no WEM).

options.content:
### NEM battery state of charge

**State of charge, power and stored energy come from AEMO; OpenElectricity supplies the fleet's identity.** AEMO's daily `Next_Day_Dispatch` report gives each unit's registered `ENERGY_STORAGE` anchor once a day (~04:11 AEST), and the 5-minute `Dispatch_SCADA` feed gives measured charge/discharge MW. The exporter anchors on the daily report and integrates the 5-minute MW between anchors (charging discounted by a fitted ~0.91 conversion efficiency), which is what makes a *live* per-unit SOC possible at all - AEMO publishes no live per-unit SOC of its own. OE never published SOC either (its ratio was derived the same way from its own stored-energy feed); what OE has that AEMO does not is the clean registered-capacity and facility metadata, so the OE exporter now exports just that - capacity, names, status and network - plus its API-budget metrics, and every number that moves is AEMO's.

**The board covers the whole AEMO fleet.** Every panel pairs the AEMO numbers with OE's capacity metadata across all dispatch units - every unit with an anchor and a SCADA stream, most of a hundred-odd units - because the SOC, power and stored-energy numbers are AEMO's and AEMO already publishes them all; the bars, the detail table and the live SCADA panels carry a DUID or facility legend and honour the Region control, not `$battery`. The join underpins it all: AEMO metrics are keyed by DUID, the OE capacity gauge by `unit`, and the codes match (`ERB01` = `ERB01`), so dividing one by the other yields % of registered capacity for any unit both sides know.

**The live SOC is an inference and this board says so.** The live SOC panels are the integrated estimate; AEMO's own daily report is not plotted. The estimate re-anchors each morning when the next daily report lands, and the drift between anchors *is* the integration error. A bar pinned at 0% or 100% is the estimate hitting its capacity bound (or the zero floor), not a battery that is empty or full. `aemo_battery_infer_success == 0` or a missing series means the exporter has no fresh anchor or the SCADA gap exceeded its 6h bridge limit, not that the battery went dark.

**Sample age is the honest companion.** Both age lines - SOC's integration and power's measurement - track the same 5-minute SCADA feed and should sit near zero; either climbing past ~15 minutes means the intraday feed stalled, and past 30 the panels above are showing the last good state, not the current one. The daily report that re-anchors the live inference arrives each morning around 04:11 AEST; nothing on the board plots the anchor age itself.

**WEM is out of scope for AEMO.** NEMWEB publishes the NEM only, so the occasional WEM battery (Collie, Synergy) on the board will simply have no AEMO series - no bar, no line, absent rather than zero. OE still tracks them in its capacity and info metrics.

**OpenElectricity is metadata-only and nearly free.** Its exporter makes one `GET /facilities/` request per refresh (daily by default) plus a free `/me` credit read - two requests a day against the free plan's 366/day bucket. It publishes the fleet's registration data (capacity, names, status) and API budget metrics; every number that moves is AEMO's.

panels.description: How many batteries AEMO is currently serving a live inferred SOC for - the units with both a daily anchor and a fresh-enough SCADA stream. This is **AEMO feed health**: a drop means the daily report is stale or the intraday feed has a gap wider than the exporter's 6h bridge limit, not that batteries have gone dark. Every AEMO unit is included.
panels.title: Batteries with a live SOC

panels.description: Registered storage capacity of every battery unit in the OpenElectricity fleet. OpenElectricity is the fleet's identity source - names, facilities and registered capacity - so this is the whole registered NEM fleet, not the AEMO-reported subset. The metric is MWh, so the query divides by 1000: in GWh the number reads at a glance, where in MWh it was a six-digit value with a 'k' buried in it.
panels.title: Fleet capacity, GWh

panels.description: The oldest sample behind any SOC number on this board, across the selected regions. Both the SOC integration and the power measurement ride the same 5-minute `Dispatch_SCADA` feed, so this should sit near zero; orange past 15 minutes (three intervals) and red past 30 means the intraday feed stalled and every panel above is showing the last good state rather than the current one. Scoped through the OE fleet map so a dispatch unit OE has never heard of cannot set the dial.
panels.title: Age of oldest reading

panels.description: How long ago the AEMO exporter finished its intraday poll - the 5-minute SCADA cycle that feeds every SOC number on this board. Green under 20m, red past 45m: the cycle runs every 5 minutes, so this is the panel that says the loop has stopped, even while every battery keeps showing its last reading.
panels.title: Since last AEMO poll

panels.description:
State of charge for every battery AEMO publishes a series for, as a percentage. Each bar is AEMO's live inferred SOC: the daily `Next_Day_Dispatch` `ENERGY_STORAGE` anchor integrated forward with 5-minute `Dispatch_SCADA` MW (charging discounted by the fitted ~0.91 conversion efficiency). AEMO publishes no live per-unit SOC of its own, so this is an estimate and it drifts between anchors - a bar pinned flat at 0% or 100% is the estimate hitting its capacity bound or zero floor, not a battery that is empty or full. It re-anchors every morning when the next daily report lands; `State of charge: live inferred (SCADA)` below plots the same estimate.

The ramp is interpolated across the bar, so it runs dark red at empty, through orange and yellow across the middle, and is green from about three-quarters full. A nearly-full battery is unambiguously green and an empty one unambiguously red, with the in-between states readable at a glance instead of having to check the number.

Batteries with no AEMO series have **no bar at all** rather than a zero-length one - a WEM unit (NEMWEB covers the NEM only) or a unit whose SCADA gap passed the exporter's 6h bridge limit simply omits the series, because an empty bar here would read as a flat battery, which is a completely different claim. Capacity comes from the whole-fleet OE metadata, so every AEMO NEM unit is eligible for a bar.
panels.title: State of charge, largest batteries first

panels.description: One row per battery AEMO publishes an inferred SOC for, joined on the unit code and sorted by registered capacity, largest first. Capacity and the identity/status labels come from the whole-fleet OE metadata; SOC, stored, sampled-at and age are AEMO's live inferred values, joined through the same capacity gauge the first column prints. Units with no AEMO series are omitted rather than shown as blank rows - a WEM battery (NEMWEB is NEM-only), a never-built committed unit, or a unit whose SCADA gap passed the exporter's bridge limit. `Sample age` should sit near zero (the feed is 5-minute); if it climbs, the SOC column is a snapshot of the last good state.

targets.expr: label_replace(max by (unit) (100 * aemo_battery_inferred_stored_mwh / on(unit) group_left(name, region, facility, status) last_over_time(oe_battery_fleet_capacity_storage_mwh{name=~"$battery",region=~"$region"}[2h])), "__name__", "SOC_pct", "", "")

panels.title: Battery detail

panels.description:
**Not an upstream reading.** Stored energy divided by 1000 so the axis reads in GWh, but the energy is AEMO's live inference: the daily `Next_Day_Dispatch` anchor integrated forward with 5-minute `Dispatch_SCADA` MW (charging discounted by the fitted ~0.91 conversion efficiency). The value is clamped to the battery's registered capacity, so a segment sitting flat at its capacity is the estimate hitting that bound, not a battery that is genuinely full.

Stacked, because the question this panel answers is how much the fleet is holding in total, and the segments show which battery is responsible. Every AEMO unit is included - the whole fleet. Two decimals rather than one: the segments span hundredths of a GWh, and at one decimal many would read 0.0.

A gap here means the inference was unavailable - no fresh anchor, or a SCADA gap wider than the exporter's 6h bridge limit - so the bars simply stop, which is a feed problem rather than a fleet holding no charge.
panels.title: Energy stored, GWh

panels.description: Daily OpenElectricity credit balance, read from the free /me endpoint each cycle. The free plan allows 500 a day; this stack is metadata-only and uses a couple.
panels.title: API credits remaining

panels.description:
Each unit's **measured** output from AEMO's `Dispatch_SCADA` archive, polled every 5-minute interval and served with the interval's age. **Negative (below zero) is charging, positive (above) is discharging** - above the line is exporting, below is absorbing - and the axis is centred on zero so the two sides compare directly. Verified off real data at 15:20 on 2026-10-08: Eraring BESS −120 MW (charging), WTAHB1 −34, LIMBESS1 +0.9.

This is the "live" view: AEMO publishes no public per-DUID live SOC, so the charge/discharge is this measured MW, and the "SoC" a NEMPulse shows is the daily reported anchor plus an integration of these 5-minute numbers (an inference, like the live SOC panels this board plots). This panel is the whole fleet by unit. A flat line here is a unit actually idle; a *gap* plus a growing `aemo_battery_power_age_seconds`, or `aemo_battery_scada_success == 0`, is a missing feed.

The **Region** filter scopes this per-unit view through the OE region map (`oe_battery_fleet_info`), the only per-unit region source - so a dispatch unit the fleet does not name drops out even under All. The AEMO exporter publishes `aemo_battery_fleet_metadata_missing` for those, so the gap is reportable rather than silent. That is the same scoping the by-region panel below and the `aemo_battery_power_mw_region` recording rule already use.
panels.title: Charge/discharge rate: live SCADA (5-min)

panels.description: The same measured `Dispatch_SCADA` output as the per-unit panel above, summed by region. `aemo_battery_power_mw_region` is a Prometheus recording rule (`prometheus_rules.yml`) that attaches a `region` label to each unit's power by joining to the OE fleet info gauge (`oe_battery_fleet_info`), so any panel can group by region without restating the join. **Negative is charging, positive is discharging.** As a cross-check this mirrors (sign-inverted) the derivative of the published per-region `aemo_battery_region_stored_mwh` - see the panel's notes above; the two disagree by whatever AEMO's reported regional storage and per-unit SCADA do.
panels.title: Charge/discharge rate by region: live SCADA (5-min)

panels.description: Per-unit state of charge dead-reckoned from the daily `Next_Day_Dispatch` ENERGY_STORAGE anchor and integrated 5-minute `Dispatch_SCADA` MW, using the same charging-leg convention as the OE exporter's inference (`charge_efficiency × |MW|×dt` when charging, `MW×dt` when discharging). Only units present in the daily anchor and within 6h of their last SCADA reading are shown (`aemo_battery_infer_success == 1` when the feed is live). Join to capacity is by DUID against the **whole-fleet** capacity gauge, so this is every unit AEMO knows. This is a complement to the region-reported aggregate, not a replacement.

targets.expr: 100 * aemo_battery_inferred_stored_mwh / on(unit) max by (unit) (oe_battery_fleet_capacity_storage_mwh) and on(unit) last_over_time(oe_battery_fleet_info{region=~"$region"}[2h])

panels.title: State of charge: live inferred (SCADA)

panels.description: Cross-check of the live inference: sum of per-unit inferred stored MWh (anchored + SCADA-integrated) versus the sum of AEMO's region-level `BDU_ENERGY_STORAGE` from `DispatchIS_Reports`. The comparison is **NEM-total only** because AEMO publishes no `REGIONID` on UNIT_SOLUTION or any per-DUID→region mapping in these intraday feeds, so per-region attribution of inferred per-unit storage is not possible without an upstream mapping (e.g. MLF/connection point data). When `aemo_battery_infer_success` drops to 0, the inferred line will span gaps or disappear; when `aemo_battery_dispatchis_success` drops to 0, the reported line will. Divergence is expected at boundaries (anchor publication) and during large gaps or feed regressions.
panels.title: Inferred vs reported storage (NEM total)

panels.description:
The region-level aggregate stored MWh from AEMO's `DispatchIS_Reports` archive, `DISPATCH,REGIONSUM` `BDU_ENERGY_STORAGE`, polled every 5-minute interval. Stacked so the top of the stack reads as the NEM's live total battery storage and the segments attribute it by region. **Reported, not inferred**: this is AEMO's own aggregate, and the only storage figure that is both live and measured across the whole fleet. Verified 15:20 on 2026-10-08: NSW1 5063.4 → 5084.6 MWh, QLD1 4238.3, SA1 1973.3, VIC1 3881.8; TAS1 has no BDU storage and publishes blanks, so it is absent by design.

It is an aggregate on purpose: AEMO reports no per-unit storage intraday, so this panel cannot be unwound into per-DUID MWh - the per-unit shares only exist in the daily snapshot. A missing segment is `aemo_battery_dispatchis_success == 0` or `aemo_battery_region_storage_interval_timestamp_seconds` drifting away from `now`.
panels.title: Stored energy by region: live (BDU)

panels.description: Gauges showing current stored energy per region (reactive units). Scaled from a fixed 0 floor to each region's own maximum (`fieldMinMax`), so a smaller region is not dwarfed by the largest one's range.
panels.title: Stored energy by region: live (BDU) gauges

panels.description:
How long the region's stored battery energy would carry the region's **current** fossil generation if the whole fossil fleet stopped at once: `stored MWh / fossil MW` (x3600 for seconds, which Grafana's time unit renders as h/d). Fanciful on every axis - it assumes lossless discharge at an unbounded rate, that fossil output is exactly the load left behind, and that nothing else picks up the slack - so read it as a mood, not a plan. It nevertheless *moves* the way one wants: it rises as batteries fill and as fossil backs off (midday solar) and falls as fossil ramps. `clamp_min` keeps a momentary zero denominator from dividing by it and the value is pinned at a week so one cannot blow the axis. Regions with no fossil units at all publish no fossil series and so have no line here.

The numerator is AEMO's reported region `BDU_ENERGY_STORAGE` (`aemo_battery_region_stored_mwh`); the denominator is measured `Dispatch_SCADA` MW attributed to coal/gas/distillate by the OE fleet cache (`aemo_battery_region_fossil_generation_mw`).
panels.title: Fossil-load runtime by region: stored MWh / fossil MW (fanciful)

panels.description: The 12 batteries charging fastest right now that still have headroom, showing % of capacity stored. Units already at or above 99% of their whole-fleet capacity are excluded *before* `topk`, since a nearly full battery can only taper its intake, not keep charging. Sign follows AEMO: `aemo_battery_power_mw < 0` is charging/absorbing, so the selection is `topk(12, -power)`. `oe_battery_fleet_capacity_storage_mwh` is the whole-fleet capacity gauge, so any dispatch unit in the SCADA panel qualifies. The dim, `(1h)` ring below each is where the unit's stored energy would sit one hour ahead at the current dispatch rate, clamped to 0..100% of capacity (`stored - power`), marked by the Point endpoint on a fixed 0-100 % scale. The **Region** filter picks the top twelve *within* the selected regions - the join sits inside the `topk`, so it is not a global twelve narrowed after.

targets.expr: 100 * aemo_battery_inferred_stored_mwh / on(unit) max by (unit) (oe_battery_fleet_capacity_storage_mwh) and on(unit) topk(12, -aemo_battery_power_mw and on(unit) (aemo_battery_power_mw < -1) and on(unit) (aemo_battery_inferred_stored_mwh < on(unit) (0.99 * max by (unit) (oe_battery_fleet_capacity_storage_mwh))) and on(unit) last_over_time(oe_battery_fleet_info{region=~"$region"}[2h]))

clamp_min(clamp_max(100 * (aemo_battery_inferred_stored_mwh - aemo_battery_power_mw) / on(unit) max by (unit) (oe_battery_fleet_capacity_storage_mwh), 100), 0) and on(unit) topk(12, -aemo_battery_power_mw and on(unit) (aemo_battery_power_mw < -1) and on(unit) (aemo_battery_inferred_stored_mwh < on(unit) (0.99 * max by (unit) (oe_battery_fleet_capacity_storage_mwh))) and on(unit) last_over_time(oe_battery_fleet_info{region=~"$region"}[2h]))

panels.title: Most active batteries (charging): stored energy vs capacity

panels.description: The 12 batteries discharging fastest right now, showing % of capacity stored. Sign follows AEMO: `aemo_battery_power_mw > 0` is discharging, so the selection is `topk(12, power)`. `oe_battery_fleet_capacity_storage_mwh` is the whole-fleet capacity gauge, so any dispatch unit in the SCADA panel qualifies. The dim, `(1h)` ring bottom row is where each unit's stored energy would sit one hour ahead at the current dispatch rate, clamped to 0..100% of its capacity (`stored - power`), marked by the Point endpoint on a fixed 0-100 % scale. The **Region** filter picks the top twelve *within* the selected regions - the join sits inside the `topk`, so it is not a global twelve narrowed after.

targets.expr: 100 * aemo_battery_inferred_stored_mwh / on(unit) max by (unit) (oe_battery_fleet_capacity_storage_mwh) and on(unit) topk(12, aemo_battery_power_mw and on(unit) last_over_time(oe_battery_fleet_info{region=~"$region"}[2h])) and on(unit) (aemo_battery_power_mw > 0)

clamp_min(clamp_max(100 * (aemo_battery_inferred_stored_mwh - aemo_battery_power_mw) / on(unit) max by (unit) (oe_battery_fleet_capacity_storage_mwh), 100), 0) and on(unit) topk(12, aemo_battery_power_mw and on(unit) last_over_time(oe_battery_fleet_info{region=~"$region"}[2h])) and on(unit) (aemo_battery_power_mw > 0)

panels.title: Most active batteries (discharging): stored energy vs capacity
